metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network degradation in a data center burns GPU-hours before it causes an outage, so fabric latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are measured continuously rather than only at failure.

The metric covers two surfaces, the facility's internal fabric and its external transit, and three quantities: round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization. Continuous measurement is the substance of it. A degrading link rarely announces itself, and it shows up as slower job completion long before it shows up as something an operator would call a fault.

For AI specifically, distributed training splits one job across many machines that must stay in step. A lossy fabric makes them wait on each other, so the cost lands as wasted compute before it lands as downtime. That is why network health sits in the same uptime category as UPS battery health, generator runtime, and SLA uptime compliance. All four protect the productivity of expensive hardware, not merely its presence.

The data defines what is watched, not what was found. There are no thresholds, no measured latency or loss values, no named facilities, and no time series. A reader cannot tell from this whether any particular fabric is healthy, only that latency, loss, and utilization are the quantities that would reveal it.
